**Category:** No change | **Verdict:** ✅ NO_CHANGE

## Verdict and consumer impact

The negative control for
`case209_calling_convention_changed_via_macro`.
v1 declares `vector_dot`/`vector_scale` with a literal
`__attribute__((ms_abi))`; v2 introduces
`#define MATHLIB_CALL __attribute__((ms_abi))` and declares
`MATHLIB_CALL double vector_dot(...)`. The declaration text changes, but the
convention it expands to does not. Both libraries are built ms_abi, so the
binary interface is identical and an unchanged old consumer works against
either — nothing for abicheck to report.

## Old/new diff

| v1.h | v2.h |
|------|------|
| `__attribute__((ms_abi)) double vector_dot(...);` | `#define MATHLIB_CALL __attribute__((ms_abi))`<br>`MATHLIB_CALL double vector_dot(...);` |

## abicheck command

```bash
gcc -shared -fPIC -g v1.c -o libv1.so
gcc -shared -fPIC -g v2.c -o libv2.so
abicheck compare libv1.so libv2.so --header old=v1.h --header new=v2.h
```

## Expected abicheck finding

```text
Verdict: NO_CHANGE (exit 0)
```

`calling_convention_changed` and `func_return_changed` must both stay
absent. Verified identically with `ABICHECK_AST_FRONTEND=castxml` and
`ABICHECK_AST_FRONTEND=clang`.

## Minimum evidence

`min_evidence: L2` — the only difference between the two versions is in the
public header text; the binaries (and their DWARF) are the same. Below the
header AST the two sides are trivially identical and the case proves nothing.

## Why abicheck catches it

abicheck compares the *effective* convention per function after macro
expansion, not the declaration's spelling. A text-level recovery that read
only the literal tokens would see `ms_abi` on the v1 side and an opaque
`MATHLIB_CALL` on the v2 side and manufacture a convention (or return-type)
change; this case pins that it does not.

## Runtime failure demonstration

There is none — that is the point of the control.

```bash
gcc -shared -fPIC -g v1.c -o libv1.so
gcc -g app.c -L. -lv1 -Wl,-rpath,'$ORIGIN' -o app -lm
./app                                    # dot product = 32.0, scaled = {2.0, 4.0, 6.0}   exit 0
gcc -shared -fPIC -g v2.c -o libv1.so    # swap in v2, no recompile
./app                                    # dot product = 32.0, scaled = {2.0, 4.0, 6.0}   exit 0
```

## Safe redesign

Nothing to redesign: routing an existing convention through a macro is a
safe refactoring as long as the macro's expansion matches the shipped
convention on every platform.

## Cross-tool comparison

```bash
abidw --out-file v1.xml libv1.so
abidw --out-file v2.xml libv2.so
abidiff v1.xml v2.xml    # no changes: the binaries are identical
```
